newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seals telecoms equipment deal with Korea.
newsitem.headline: EU seals telecoms equipment deal with Korea.

text.p: The European Union and South Korea have struck a deal to throw open their telecommunications equipment markets to each other's suppliers, the European Commission said on Monday.

"European companies will now be treated as fairly as their Korean counterparts when bidding for contracts to supply telecoms equipment to the network run by Korea Telecom," the EU executive said in a statement.
The deal, sealed over the weekend by the Commission and the Korean government, will also give Korean suppliers equal access to contracts in Europe's $22-billion-a-year market.
The Commission said it would withdraw the dispute procedure begun against Korea in the World Trade Organisation if EU ministers, who have the final say on the accord, give it a green light.

The deal covers contracts in Korea's $6 billion telecoms equipment market awarded by both state-controlled Korea Telecom and by newly licensed private operators, the Commission said. Korea Telecom accounts for 80 percent of the country's telecoms network market.
"Today's breakthrough, which follows over two years of intense negotiations, applies mainly to switching and transmission equipment and cables," the Commission said.

Korea pledged to end legislation and practices that discriminate against European products, while the Commission agreed that the EU would waive a provision in its "utilities directive" that gives preference to European telecoms products.

That directive allows public agencies to reject bids when products are less than 50 percent EU origin. It also requires them to prefer EU bids over other equivalent bids if the price difference is no more than three percent.

Suppliers will have the right to challenge contract awards in national courts and the two sides will use a binding dispute-settlement mechanism to settle disagreements over implementation of the accord, it said.

The Commission said the deal should make it easier to conclude the proposed global would Information Technology Agreement, which aims to eliminate tariffs on a wide range of computer and telecommunications equipment.
